output.summary: The architectural center is an immutable Diagram revision model composed into versioned canvases. Browser editing, agent tools, isolated change proposals, and evaluation workflows converge on shared canvas commands and history, while filesystem adapters publish durable records. Fifteen anchors capture these responsibilities, their ownership boundaries, and the separate static-analysis tooling. Review depth varied: every inventoried file received a source-text structural skim, with implementation-level tracing concentrated on these anchors.

points.title: Application Composition and Transports
points.rationale: The server bootstrap selects concrete repositories, agent runtimes, and services, connects their ports, and disposes their resources. The Vite adapter mounts HTTP and WebSocket interfaces. Architecture tests enforce the domain/application/infrastructure/UI boundaries, making this the clearest entry point for understanding dependency direction.

relationships.label: constructs and injects filesystem repositories
wires canvas bridges and mounts agent transports
constructs chat service and disposes its connection
connects generation, comparison, and experiment services

points.title: Immutable Diagram Revisions
points.rationale: Diagram is the shared content boundary: stable diagram identity, immutable revision identity, ASCII content, source evidence, mappings, highlights, and jumps travel together. Revision operations validate edits and preserve explicit node continuity; the registry rejects conflicting payloads under an existing identity. Canvas placement remains outside this content model.

relationships.label: builds and validates parsed content and node identities

points.title: ASCII Structure and Anchors
points.rationale: This boundary turns ASCII into addressable structure used by selection, folding, source mapping, and connection endpoints. Parser versions preserve compatibility with stored content. Tree content carries its parsed structure, while graph content exposes a cached derived node index; the spatial interpreter retains source spans and interpretation evidence.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: MappingDocumentController is the common mutation facade for live editing and headless proposals. CanvasHistory owns checkpoints, diagram revision bindings, branching, undo/redo, and saved views. Commands validate versions and complete their changes before publishing a checkpoint. LineGrid separates reusable diagram content from hierarchical placements and layout.

relationships.label: retains issued revisions through checkpoint bindings
uses content nodes to validate and reconcile anchors

points.title: Browser Workspace Ownership
points.rationale: CanvasWorkspace owns canvas session lifetimes; each CanvasSession exposes separate subscriptions for document, presentation, selection, controls, geometry, and status. WorkspacePersistence translates committed changes into incremental records, while RecordStorage coalesces writes and retries ambiguous failures with the identical request. This explains how many open canvases share persistence without publishing every pointer movement.

relationships.label: creates session controllers and retains editing contexts
sends versioned record batches through workspace HTTP
mounts an editor for each canvas session

points.title: Native Canvas Interaction
points.rationale: The tldraw Editor owns live geometry and native undo navigation. MappingEditorRuntime projects semantic state into shapes and commits settled gestures back to the controller. CanvasRuntime keeps renderer-local models, measurements, connection focus, and routing resources. This is an important ownership boundary between interactive frames and durable semantic changes.

relationships.label: commits gestures and restores semantic checkpoints
consumes the mounted canvas session
uses revision-scoped nodes for rendered anchors

points.title: Durable Records and Publication
points.rationale: Persistence distinguishes the editable workspace from published catalog representations. WorkspaceRecordStore writes content-addressed records before atomically replacing a manifest containing revision guards and retry receipts. Catalog publication can pin an already persisted checkpoint without expanding its entire archive. DiagramStore supplies the shared repository facade.

relationships.label: persists checkpoint graphs, composition, and view records
stores immutable revisions before publishing references

points.title: Repository Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source resolution follows an explicit diagram source binding instead of assuming a project has one repository. Mapping joins resolve selected diagram nodes to captured source ranges, retaining provenance and hashes. Corpus and language-service adapters provide file access and definition lookup, while CodePanel translates these joins into the browsing experience.

relationships.label: resolves source bindings, mappings, and captured evidence
reads registered sources and published representations

points.title: Agent Canvas Access
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService binds tool operations to specific canvases or proposals, resolves compact read aliases, enforces access modes, and handles retries. CanvasSessionBridge dispatches commands to browser owners; LiveCanvasService tracks publishers, selection deltas, and reader identities. MCP and HTTP expose this shared application boundary.

relationships.label: dispatches commands to the owning browser workspace
routes proposal-scoped reads and mutations
starts diagram edits and atomic generation batches
resolves uploaded and saved agent contexts

points.title: Reusable Agent Contexts
points.rationale: AgentContext is a validated, hashed conversation value with coherent tool-call history and pinned source references. AgentContextLibrary manages durable creation, forks, comments, and discovery. Source adapters choose committed Git content or immutable snapshots and can produce portable selected-range exports. This is the reusable input boundary shared by editing and evaluations.

relationships.label: captures source ranges through repository and corpus bindings
binds compiled context to diagram identity and source fingerprint

points.title: Validated Diagram Generation
points.rationale: DiagramEditService pins target revisions, resolves prompt references and contexts, generates candidates, and applies them only through a version-checked canvas port. Batch generation stages multiple operations before one application. The runtime accepts output through a validating submission tool and owns cancellation and session cleanup; issuing a revision remains a domain operation.

relationships.label: validates candidate edits and issues immutable revisions
loads pinned context and captures successful conversation history
uses supplied canvas ports for snapshots and acknowledged application

points.title: Agent Chat Lifecycle
points.rationale: AgentChatService owns persistent conversations, turn deduplication, streaming events, pending questions, and turn-bound canvas access. StdioCodexConnection owns the external app-server process and RPC lifecycle. GenerationCanvasBridge gives background alternatives isolated controller-backed canvases, allowing chat generation to reuse canvas operations without editing the live source canvas.

relationships.label: invokes tools with the canvas captured for the active turn
owns isolated controllers for generation candidates
reuses saved context for background generation

points.title: Isolated Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository commits, hunks, and canvas baselines into isolated proposals. Proposal edits use the shared controller and retain their own history and receipts. Acceptance checks both live and published baselines before publishing affected canvases. The two-step workflow and push integration provide automated entry paths into this review boundary.

relationships.label: applies proposal edits through isolated controller histories
publishes accepted canvases with durable acceptance receipts
pins repository context and captures Git hunks
exposes scoped tools to the materialization workflow

points.title: Generation Experiments and Evaluation
points.rationale: EvalRunService coordinates repeatable workflows over pinned canvas inputs, prompt versions, references, and AgentContexts. ExperimentService prepares and launches reviewed plans; comparison capture preserves selected checkpoints independently of later source changes. Materializers turn validated model output into canvases, while judgements and promotion connect evaluation results back to published work.

relationships.label: pins context hashes and resolves model-visible evidence
captures checkpoints and materializes generated canvases
publishes promoted outputs into the project catalog
reconciles chat-generated alternatives into evaluation runs

points.title: Static Architecture Analysis
points.rationale: A separate CLI-driven pipeline extracts declarations, lexical references, calls, resource ownership, framework relationships, and dataflow from TypeScript. It derives partitions, metrics, components, and findings with source provenance. IncrementalAnalyzer owns reusable component fragments and broadens invalidation for uncertain global effects. This is a substantial independent subsystem, not an established browser generation stage.

relationships.label: shares source-layer classification with architecture boundary tests

limitations: This was not a complete line-by-line reading of the 7.28 MB snapshot. reviewedPaths includes files inspected through source-text excerpts: declarations, imports, method names, test descriptions, or opening statements. Detailed implementation reading concentrated on the selected architectural paths; many leaf components, tests, styles, scripts, benchmarks, Python parser utilities, and projection-3d files received only a structural skim.
Relationships describe source-supported dependencies and invocation paths, not observed runtime traces. Tests and the application were not executed.

The assessment is limited to the pinned working-tree snapshot. The index excludes corpus data, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor dependencies, node_modules, most documentation, binary assets, and lockfiles.
Secondary responsibilities such as file compaction, local selection chat, search, treemaps, migrations, and the 3D prototype remain expansion candidates rather than separate initial anchors.
